label: Unemployment rate
description: The percentage of the labour force who are unemployed and actively seeking work. Seasonally adjusted.
explainer: The unemployment rate is one of the most watched economic indicators — governments live and die by it politically. Australia's rate peaked at 11.2% during the 1990–91 recession and fell to a 50-year low of 3.4% in 2023. Note that the official rate undercounts labour market distress — it excludes 'underemployed' workers (those working fewer hours than they want) and people who have given up looking. The underemployment rate is typically 2–3x higher.
projection_source: RBA Statement on Monetary Policy. Projects unemployment rising moderately to 4.5% by end 2026 as the economy slows.
